recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which power of x you divide by, and what happens to the remaining terms.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide throughout by x²
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the highest power and divide by it. Writing "∞/∞" on its own earns nothing.
lines: As x → ∞ both lines increase without bound, so this is the indeterminate form ∞/∞.
The highest power of x present is x². Divide every term of both lines by x² (x ≠ 0):

recall.must_convey: That the numerator and denominator are each divided by x², the highest power of x.
accept: divide the top and the bottom by x squared
x squared is the highest power so divide by it
take x squared common from both lines
x square tho rendu lines ni divide cheyyali
divide throughout by the highest power of x

steps.why: Substitution gives the indeterminate form ∞/∞. Dividing by the highest power turns every remaining term into one of the form c/xⁿ, and each of those approaches 0, so the value can then be read off.
common_mistakes: Dividing by x instead of x², which leaves an x in both lines.
steps.memory_tip: The same highest power on both lines means the answer is the ratio of the two leading coefficients.

steps.label: Let each 1/x term approach 0
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Box 1/2 — the coefficient of x² on top over the coefficient of x² below.

recall.must_convey: That every term of the form c/xⁿ approaches 0, leaving 1/2.
accept: all the one over x terms go to zero leaving one over two
only the x squared coefficients survive so it is one by two
one by x terms zero ayipothayi, one by two vasthundi
the limit is zero point five

steps.why: Each term of the form c/xⁿ approaches 0 as x increases without bound, so only the two leading coefficients remain.
common_mistakes: Giving 2, by writing the ratio of coefficients upside down.
Keeping 5/x in the final answer instead of letting it approach 0.
steps.memory_tip: Coefficient of x² on top over coefficient of x² below: 1 over 2.
